scope.summary: One PostgreSQL 16 runtime substrate for the MetaFramer Kernel: schema baseline under Alembic, FORCE row-level security bound to a fail-closed transaction-local tenant context, explicit transaction boundaries, a transactional outbox with a safe concurrent claim, and an append-only audit trail.
scope.runtimeTablesNote: This package owns exactly two runtime tables, named here as they exist in the database. No business or domain table is invented: a substrate package has no domain, so transaction-boundary and row-level-security behaviour is exercised against the tables the substrate itself owns. Every row-level-security obligation below is enumerated over precisely this list.
scope.phaseAScope: Test harness, pinned dependency lock, deterministic real PostgreSQL 16 Docker lifecycle, this contract, its fail-closed verifier, repository script integration, and failing behavioural tests. Nothing else.
scope.phaseBScope: The production substrate that turns the Phase A tests green. Not authorized to be written until Phase A RED is accepted.

rollback.trigger: the pinned Actionplan authority, the pinned kernel base commit, the digest-pinned activation base, the declared production surface, or the not-effective package state drifts
rollback.action: run `alembic downgrade base` with metaframer_kernel_db.migrations.alembic_config against every database the substrate was applied to, then revert db/, tools/check-kernel-runtime-substrate-s1.mjs, tests/kernel-runtime-substrate-s1.test.mjs and the package.json and .gitignore wiring as one logical shard
rollback.blastRadius: the substrate schema and the package: both runtime tables with their policies and indexes, the append-only trigger, the context key table and the four attestation functions. pgcrypto is a shared database-level object and is deliberately left in place.
rollback.runtimeDataImpact: DESTRUCTIVE. The downgrade drops transactional_outbox and audit_log, so every outbox row and every audit record in that database is permanently lost; unclaimed rows are discarded undelivered and the audit trail cannot be reconstructed. Dropping mfk_context_key destroys the per-database signing key, so any attestation minted before the rollback is worthless afterwards. Take a backup before rolling back any database holding real data.
rollback.dependentCode: none: no primitive, SDK, app, module or surface consumes this substrate yet, so reverting it breaks no caller
rollback.reversibilityNote: The code rollback is clean; the data rollback is not. On this branch the substrate has only ever been applied to per-test containers that are destroyed either way, so the destructive impact is prospective — it applies from the first durable deployment onward, not to anything that exists today.
rollback.note: Phase A could claim a rollback with no runtime data impact because no schema existed. That is no longer true and this block no longer says it: a substrate that owns an audit trail cannot be un-applied without destroying one.

This substrate package neither owns any of the three boundaries nor writes to them; it only re-exports the shared root-source-topology fence. An absent root src stays fully compliant, and this checkout materializes src/domain for P-M1-01, src/application for P-M1-02 and src/sdk for the generated-SDK generation package. No first child remains forbidden by name, and any unclassified first child still fails closed. Nothing beneath src/domain, src/application, src/sdk, src/adapters or src/delivery is classified by this clause, and the narrowing moves no authority, readiness or activation value. The rule is stated once in tools/check-repository-boundary.mjs and read from there by this package.

staticAnalysis.command: cd db && uv lock --check && uv run --frozen ruff check metaframer_kernel_db tests && uv run --frozen ruff format --check metaframer_kernel_db tests && PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mfk-substrate-s1-pycache" uv run --frozen python -m compileall -q metaframer_kernel_db tests
staticAnalysis.note: The static toolchain is pinned in db/pyproject.toml and resolved exactly in db/uv.lock, and every step runs through `uv run --frozen` from that resolved environment. An ephemeral `uvx ruff` would lint with whatever version the machine happened to fetch, which is not a reproducible check and is refused here. Ruff's settings live in db/pyproject.toml so the commands carry no flags and two people running them get the same answer. compileall writes its bytecode to PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX outside the working tree, so the check leaves no artifact behind to be tracked.

redFollowUps.note: Both follow-ups were declared RED and failing, and are now implemented. The key keeps its name because that is where they came from: each gap records the RED that specified it and the GREEN that satisfied it, and the verifier now enforces the opposite of what it enforced before — the implementations must be present, and a contract still claiming they are absent fails the run.

gaps.statement: The shipped release and publish paths take identifiers only, so they cannot distinguish the current claimant of a row from a previous one. After a lease expires and a second claimant reclaims the row, the stale claimant can still release the live claim back to the queue or mark work published that is still in progress. A fenced API compares the caller's claim token against the one stored on the row and affects zero rows when they differ.

declaredCapabilities.contract: release_claim(connection, ids, *, claim_token) -> list[id] releasing only rows whose stored claim token equals claim_token, inside the caller's transaction and tenant context
declaredCapabilities.proves: a stale claimant cannot hand a live claim back to the queue

declaredCapabilities.contract: publish_claim(connection, ids, *, claim_token) -> list[id] marking published only rows whose stored claim token equals claim_token, inside the caller's transaction and tenant context
declaredCapabilities.proves: a stale claimant cannot record work as finished that another claimant is still doing

assertions: a stale claimant's fenced release affects zero rows and leaves the current claim's token, claimed_at and claim_expires_at untouched
a stale claimant's fenced publish affects zero rows and leaves the row unpublished and the current claim intact
the current claim token can release its own claim, after which the row is unclaimed and returns to circulation

a fenced mutation never crosses the tenant boundary: tenant A holding tenant B's genuine current token still affects zero rows, because row-level security denies the row before any token is compared
gaps.boundaryNote: The package offers no unfenced mutation path: both public mutations require a claim token and raise rather than default when one is absent. Raw SQL remains available to whoever holds the table grant — that is what a grant means — and row-level security is what constrains it, denying another tenant's row before any token is compared. Per-statement authorisation of a caller that legitimately holds the grant is the policy decision point's job, not the substrate's.

gaps.statement: Activation currently has predicates but no deterministic evaluator, and no compositor to turn one into a single authoritative line. The record of activation must be one annotated Git tag created by the root Codex MASTER after merge and published on the canonical origin, never an in-repository status flip, never a commit that records its own hash, and never a tag that exists only locally.

tagAuthority.note: A tag that exists only in a working copy proves nothing: anyone holding the checkout can create one, so a local tag is evidence about that machine, not about the project. The activation record is the tag object published on the canonical origin, and the reader must confirm it is there. That confirmation is a bounded remote lookup; if it errors, times out, finds nothing, or finds a tag object that differs from the local one, the answer is that the package is not effective. It is never a failure of the check itself — an unreachable network must not be able to activate anything, and must not be able to break the run either.

rootProcedure: 1. Root Codex MASTER merges the package to Kernel main through the normal review gate; the writer never merges.
2. Root Codex MASTER checks out the exact origin/main commit, having first verified the remote identity is the canonical Kernel repository.
3. Root Codex MASTER runs npm test, npm run check, npm run check:substrate-s1:static and npm run test:substrate-s1 on that checkout and records the results.

4. Only if all four are GREEN, root Codex MASTER creates the annotated tag kernel-runtime-substrate-s1-activated on the verified package commit, with the strict structured message binding the package id, the package commit, the independent verification identity and the exact commands and their GREEN results.
5. Root Codex MASTER pushes the tag to the canonical origin. Until that push lands the tag is local and activates nothing. No status-flip commit is made and no commit records its own hash.

6. Any later verifier run resolves the tag object on the canonical origin through a bounded lookup and computes effectiveness deterministically; it never asks a repository file whether it is effective, and it treats an unreachable origin as not-effective rather than as an error.
